text:
maria: Heads up — multiple customers (acme-prod, beta-ops) hit 503s + p95 latency spike starting ~09:10 UTC. Customer support opened tickets, they see errors from the API gateway. Posting initial probe notes here.
ash: Can you paste the gateway error sample and the upstream error id? Is it auth/billing or upstream worker failures?
maria: Gateway log sample attached in ticket: `upstream_error_id=urn:inf:pool-6:worker-23` and response `503 Service Unavailable`. Customer says it started right after a deploy window. Not auth/billing.
sre-bot: ALERT hosted-infer pool-6: worker-restarts=27 window=09:10-09:18 severity=high // link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/5902
samir: I pulled node and pod events for pool-6, seeing repeated container restarts with OOM and a segfault before each restart. Short excerpts:
```
Oct 05 09:11:02 node-12 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (infer-runner) score 987 or sacrifice child
2026-10-05T09:11:03Z infer-runner[4123]: fatal error: signal 11 (SIGSEGV), address 0x7ff...
stderr: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 3.2 GiB
```
samir: Also saw autoscaler pull/concurrency jitter — some pods dropped from 8 -> 2 concurrent contexts around 09:09 which likely increased per-pod load.
elaine: We rolled quantized-ggml-large-v2 into pool-6 at 08:55 as a canary. Model uses larger KV memory on long contexts — could be lower memory headroom on those GPUs.
nash: That aligns: model swap increased memory footprint per request, autoscaler reacted by reducing concurrency, which then increased queueing and larger batches -> OOM.
maria: Customer-facing status: "We're investigating elevated 5xxs and latency, suspected upstream inference restarts. ETA unknown." They asked for repro steps.
samir: Short-term mitigation applied: drained pool-6 from routing, scaled up fallback pool (pool-3), and disabled the new canary model rollout. Doing rolling restart of workers with constrained concurrency=2 and disabled prefetch.
elaine: Reverted model on pool-6 at 09:20. After revert we saw restart rate drop and 503s from gateway dropped to baseline by 09:28.
nash: Repro notes for engineering: steps to trigger locally on staging (approx):
1) Deploy quantized-ggml-large-v2 to staging pool.
2) Set pod concurrency=8 and prefetch enabled.
3) Send sustained streaming toolcall load with long context (~8k tokens) at ~200 qps.
Expected: OOM in 30–90s and segfaults/restarts on some pods.
Relevant logs to capture: `infer-runner.log` (stderr), `dmesg` (OOM killer), and `nvml` resets.
eli: (action) I'll open a follow-up: infra to add a canary step verifying peak GPU memory under intended concurrency, and runtime to add pre-deploy safety check for model memory estimate.
maria: Customer update posted at 09:35: "We rolled back the recent model change and routed traffic away from affected capacity. Services are recovering; we'll share a postmortem." :thumbsup:
samir: Followups created: issue #INF-8023 (canary memory check), #INF-8024 (autoscaler backpressure tuning). I'll add short-term runbook tweak: force-concurrency cap for new model deployments.
nash: FYI for oncall: if you see pool restart spikes again, immediate steps = 1) add pool to fallback routing, 2) scale pool down and disable prefetch, 3) revert recent model swap, 4) collect full core dump + nvml logs and tag incident channel.
maria: Thanks everyone — handing off to infra + runtime for deeper triage. I'll keep customers updated with the followup links.
